misconceptions.description: Believing aggregate utility is the only criterion for an AI deployment decision
misconceptions.trigger: learner argues 'net benefit is positive, ship it'
misconceptions.feedback: Aggregate metrics hide distribution. Deontology and care ethics resist sacrificing concentrated harm for aggregate gain. Triangulate.

misconceptions.description: Reducing virtue ethics to vague niceness rather than the systematic question of cultivated habits
misconceptions.trigger: learner equates virtue ethics with 'be nice'
misconceptions.feedback: Virtue ethics asks which habits and dispositions the technology cultivates in its users over time. It is the framework most equipped to name deskilling, manipulation, and erosion of judgment.

misconceptions.description: Equating care ethics with paternalistic 'deciding for' the vulnerable
misconceptions.trigger: learner dismisses care ethics as patronizing
misconceptions.feedback: Care ethics attends to vulnerability and relationships without overriding agency. The risk of paternalism is real and the framework names it explicitly; it is not the framework's content.

misconceptions.description: Committing to one ethical framework and treating other frameworks' verdicts as noise
misconceptions.trigger: learner cites only their preferred framework when frameworks disagree
misconceptions.feedback: Frameworks have blind spots. Convergence across frameworks is what makes a decision defensible; disagreement is the live decision and should be documented, not hidden.
